video.title: Milwaukee Bucks Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]

summary: Josh Lloyd previews the 2026/27 Milwaukee Bucks, the team's first season without Giannis. He says it is the roster he is least sure about, with too many guards, a new coach in Taylor Jenkins, no control of their own draft pick and a likely shift toward developing young players. His projected starting five is Ryan Rollins, Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner, with Kevin Porter Jr. as sixth man and Kel'el Ware as backup center. His best draft target is Ryan Rollins, whom ESPN undervalues. His biggest fade is Myles Turner at his current ADP, and his late swing is Kevin Porter Jr. He calls Herro reasonable around pick 60, would avoid Kuzma inside the top 200, and advises against drafting rookie Brayden Burries in standard leagues.

rules.text: Unpredictable teams and rotations that change often are bad for fantasy value.
rules.quote: It's just everything screams bad for fantasy. Unpredictable is never great.

rules.text: A team that does not own its draft pick has no reason to tank, but it may still give young players more minutes to develop them.
rules.quote: don't have control of their draft pick. So, that's not a motivation.

rules.text: Do not treat a big man as a top player just because of high block numbers.
rules.quote: people were looking at, wow, the high block numbers that means you're a top 20 player.

rules.text: Site ADPs can be too high for weak players simply because they start, given how sites build their ADPs.
rules.quote: I think the ADPs are high because of the way that these sites have to roll their ADPs out.

rules.text: Rookies rarely give standard league value, even when they get a steady rotation role. Treat them as stashes.
rules.quote: even if he finds a regular every night rotation role, rookies just really can't do that most of the time.

rules.text: Late-season rookie breakouts used to come against tanking teams. With fewer teams not trying, those chances will be harder.
rules.quote: There's just not going to be those teams that aren't trying.

rules.text: Note a rookie's age. Older rookies have a different development outlook.
rules.quote: So, he's like two years in college player. Just sometimes it's worth being aware of that.
